aqi: US EPA PM2.5 breakpoints (2024). PurpleAir series are EPA-corrected; the regulatory series is the official 24-hour concentration converted with the same breakpoints (no PurpleAir correction).

sources.label: School-area sensor (#322702)
sources.note: Daily mean of EPA-corrected (Barkjohn 2021 / AirNow piecewise) 24-hour PurpleAir PM2.5, converted with the current U.S. EPA PM2.5 AQI breakpoints.

sources.label: Earlier nearby outdoor sensors (~0.7–1.4 km from the facility)
sources.note: Mostly sensor #52853 (from 17 Apr 2020 through 30 Apr 2026, ~1.4 km from the facility). Gaps after that, through 26 Oct 2026, are filled from sensor #289878 (~0.7 km). These are not the school-area sensor and are labeled separately. No near-facility outdoor PurpleAir record was found before 17 Apr 2020.

sources.label: Other nearby sensors' median
sources.note: Daily median EPA-corrected AQI of the outdoor comparison sensors then online (the same nearby set used on this page, plus one earlier outdoor sensor at a similar distance that stopped in 2023). Membership changes as sensors start or stop. This is an area comparison, not a background regulatory monitor.

sources.label: BAAQMD Jackson St, San Jose (~17 km)
sources.note: The long-running Fremont regulatory monitor has no published PM2.5 daily values in 2020–2026. This is the nearest BAAQMD/EPA monitor with a nearly complete daily PM2.5 record. Official 2025–2026 daily values were not yet in EPA’s public daily files when this was built. AQI uses the current (2024) U.S. EPA PM2.5 breakpoints. This is a different source and location from the school-area PurpleAir sensor.

theil_sen_near_facility.method: Theil-Sen on monthly mean EPA-corrected AQI (near-facility series: school-area sensor when present, otherwise the earlier nearby outdoor sensor). August–September 2020 wildfire-smoke days are excluded.

takeaways: Near-facility daily mean EPA-corrected AQI (wildfire-smoke days in August–October 2020 excluded), by year: 2020: 46.5, 2021: 37.1, 2022: 37.4, 2023: 33.3, 2024: 31.8, 2025: 31.7, 2026: 32.9. These are annual averages of daily values, not a finding about any single source.

A Theil-Sen trend on monthly means (smoke days excluded) for the near-facility series is about -0.98 AQI per year over 68 months. The school-area sensor itself only starts in late 2026 (first daily value 2 Oct 2026), so this longer slope mostly reflects an earlier nearby outdoor sensor (~1.4 km from the facility) plus a short recent overlap. A slope is not a cause, and wildfire years still need to be read with care.

Yearly mean of (near-facility AQI minus the other-sensors median) is 2020: +8.9, 2021: +5.5, 2022: +6.9, 2023: +5.7, 2024: +7.6, 2025: +8.2, 2026: +9.6. A positive number means the near-facility reading was higher than the local median that year, on average; it does not identify a source.

When a day’s near-facility reading was 30 AQI or more above the other-sensors median, wind came from the facility direction more often in some years (2026: on 7 days with a near-facility excess of 30+ AQI, wind was from the facility direction 71% of the time, versus 15% on other days). This is a correlation only, not evidence that the facility caused those readings. Light winds make direction less certain.

Averaged across years (smoke days excluded), the near-facility daily AQI is highest in Dec (44.1) and lowest in Mar (23.8). Winter stagnation and summer wildfire smoke (when not excluded) both matter in this region.

Official suspicious-spike counts (10-minute AQI of 76 or higher, or a jump of 35 or more) are only available where 10-minute data is on file: 2026: 18. Earlier years show “no 10-minute data,” not zero spikes.

The school-area sensor (#322702) is registered from 27 Aug 2026; its first daily value in this archive is 2026-10-02. An earlier nearby outdoor sensor (~1.4 km from the facility, #52853) covers 17 Apr 2020 through 29 Apr 2026, with a large gap in spring–summer 2024. No near-facility outdoor PurpleAir record was found from January through mid-April 2020. Official regulatory PM2.5 for 2025–2026 was not yet in EPA’s public daily files. Gaps are shown as “no data,” not as zeros.
Nothing here claims that the Tesla Fremont facility caused a reading. Compare series, start dates, and annotated smoke periods before drawing conclusions.
